newsitem.title: RUSSIA: LUKoil to get 10 percent of Chevron stake.
newsitem.headline: LUKoil to get 10 percent of Chevron stake.

text.p: Russia's biggest oil company, NK LUKoil, said Thursday it completed talks with Chevron Corp. to acquire 10 percent of the U.S. oil company's stake in the $20 billion Tengiz oil project in Kazakhstan.
Chevron Corp. owns 50 percent in TengizChevroil, or TCO, while Mobil Corp and the Kazakh government each own 25 percent.
LUKoil's purchase from San Francisco-based Chevron of a 10 percent stake would give it a 5 percent share in the joint venture.

A statement quoted LUKoil Vice-President Dzevhan Cheloyants as saying Russia's biggest oil company and Chevron had reached mutual understanding on all basic conditions of the agreement. It gave no other details.
LUKoil President Vagit Alekperov said Wednesday that LUKoil expected to conclude the terms of the purchase by early February.
Tengiz, in western Kazakhstan, has estimated crude oil reserves of six to nine billion barrels. Output is already at around 160,000 barrels per day and is expected to rise to 700,000 by 2010.
